previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with worsening nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and abdominal pain, following a recent hospitalization for similar symptoms. She has a complex history including chronic graft-versus-host disease, gastroparesis, and immunosuppression. Initial evaluation revealed metabolic acidosis and leukocytosis. Imaging showed no acute abdominal pathology but mild colitis on MRI. Stool testing confirmed rotavirus infection, explaining her gastroenteritis. She also had a complicated UTI with Enterococcus, treated with nitrofurantoin. During her stay, she received IV fluids, antiemetics, and supportive care, with gradual improvement. She tolerated oral intake, and symptoms resolved. A sacral bone marrow finding on MRI prompted a recommendation for outpatient pelvic MRI to rule out infiltrative disease. She was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up plans, including completing antibiotics, restarting bowel regimen when appropriate, and coordinating outpatient imaging and IVIG.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mrs. ___ is a ___ yo woman with myeloblastic CML s/p allogeneic 
stem cell transplant with chronic GVHD on chronic prednisone, 
monthly IVIG infusions, who presented with syncope of unclear 
etiology.

# Syncope: Patient lost consciousness in the setting of feeling 
lightheaded. She had LOC and received chest compressions, 
although not clear whether she had a pulse throughout the event. 
She awoke rather quickly and had BP's in 50's systolic, which 
appeared to be responsive to fluids and steroids in the ED. She 
was seen by Cardiology, who did not feel EKG to be c/w ACS, 
especially in setting of negative trops. They noted slightly 
prolonged QT, but with arrhythmia unlikely to cause her 
prodromal symptoms. She was monitored closely on tele, without 
any noted abnormalities. She had CT chest to r/o PE and had 
blood cultures drawn to w/o Infection (all NGTD on discharge). 
On the floors, she was found at times to have low blood 
pressures in the 90's systolic and was orthostatic, consistent 
with hypovolemia as likely cause of syncope, although vasovagal 
is also a possibility. She received IV fluids and on day of 
discharge she denied any lightheadedness and was ambulating 
without difficulty.  

#Myeloblastic CML s/p stem cell transplant; Ms. ___ has a hx 
of myeloblastic CML s/p allogeneic stem cell transplant in ___, 
complicated by development of GVHD. For her GVHD she is on 
chronic immunosuppression with daily prednisone and monthly 
IVIG. She is on several prophylactic antibiotics and 
antifungals, which were all initially continued during this 
admission. After discussion with her outpatient ___ provider and 
by recommendation of Cardiology, who noted prolonged QTc on EKG, 
fluconazole was not continued in hospital or at discharge. She 
was also maintained on other home medications to treat her GVHD 
symptoms (notably her autologous serum eyedrops and cyclosporine 
eyedrops).
 
# Vertebral body compression fractures: On CT chest to r/o PE, 
incidental findings of mild C7 and T2 vertebral body compression 
deformities were noted. Age of these fractures were 
indeterminate although they both were new since ___. T2 
deformity was noted on imaging study in ___. Neurosurgery 
saw Ms. ___ in ED, did not feel these to be significant enough 
to warrant C-collar. Patient was also asymptomatic, without any 
C-spine tenderness to palpation, pain, or limited ROM. Not an 
active issue during hospitalization.
